text.p: Reigning 500cc world champion Michael Doohan held off Honda team mates Tadayuki Okada and Alex Criville in Saturday's qualifying for the Austrian Grand Prix to clinch the 40th pole position of his career.
The Australian championship leader snatched pole five minutes before the end of the hour-long session by clocking one minute 28.803 -- 0.310 ahead of Okada and 0.507 in front of Criville.
Japan's Okada crashed heavily with only three minutes of qualifying remaining in a final attempt to better Doohan's time and sustained bruising to the left hip.
After Okada had been X-rayed, officials at the A1-Ring said he would be able to compete in Sunday's race.
Okada went into both qualifying sessions with a painful left wrist which he injured in the Italian Grand Prix two weeks ago.
Spain's Carlos Checa, also riding a Honda, posted a time of 1:29.399 to complete the front row of the grid. All four men were inside the circuit best of 1:29.430 set by Doohan in 1996.

Doohan, who has won three of the first four grands prix of the season, said: "I didn't go out and gun for a 1:28 time. I don't think the race will be run this fast. Race laps will be in the high 1:29s."
Criville, who trails Doohan in the standings by 17 points, was markedly better than on Friday when he managed only a seventh best time.
"Yesterday I had problems with the front suspension but today I found a set-up which is not perfect but works quite well," said Criville, last year's winner.
Yamaha rider Luca Cadalora prevented Honda from claiming the top eight positions on the grid with the fifth-best qualifying time of 1:29.688.
